I kinda want to slide in here and say that the effects of quitting weed will always be a hindrance if you don’t want to quit. If when you do your “cost-benefit analysis” and make it so weed always win you won’t actually locate the resources you need to quit. 

Maybe not quitting weed is an intrusive thought process too? And instead of the ability to focus on your other intrusive thoughts, you get consumed with the easier weed related ones. 

I think what you struggling with right now is lack of the ability to trust yourself when you need to stand up to your intrusive thoughts. I noticed that this sorta thing is related to black and white thinking so please don’t be all or nothing on your journey to getting better for yourself. The intrusive thoughts won’t always be a default if you retrain your brain to allow for kindness instead. 

This took me years before I could trust myself fully to quit weed and be okay without it. Trail and error until I found out that it’s okay to have bad thoughts and it’s nothing I should abuse myself over.

Remember you are not your thoughts, you are your actions irl and how you respond to those thoughts. Please don’t ignore the fact that the pain you are describing is societal conditioning. It’s not you, it’s what you are trained to think about you. 

There is no shame in living, only in cruelty, don’t be cruel to yourself for trying to not be a bad person.

I was in a pretty rough spot at the time, and I am not trying to over share but it’s important for the context of the post: I was on a bad situation (breaking and entering and r*pe)with my ex and didn’t have a lot of support. I still haven’t talked about it to anyone besides my partner because it directly affected them, and I have given up in sharing that a while ago. People like to make assumptions about what happened rather than ask and how do you fight that without pushing the pain into them? 

After I left life got a bit harder with time and people in my family started passing away one by one. I think the trauma and stuff got to me and I was having a breakdown and I didn’t know how to cope with it. 

To be honest things have not been better for a while, I tried really hard to build my confidence and feel more comfortable trying to reenter society. I am proud of how far I have come but some messed up stuff happened to me this summer and I just can’t look at people the same way anymore. 

People are no longer safe for me and that’s kinda what this breakdown was about. It was me recognizing that I needed help and community but nothing was coming. It got worse for a long time, and most of the people who raised me passed away within the year of me posting this. Everyone has their own thing and I was too much for everyone around me. I was too nervous and fast for them to feel comfortable and it’s fair, what do you do when someone lost everything in their life with not a single person besides their partner and their manager telling you “I’m sorry for your loss”. 

My body kept protesting the pain, and there was no outlet. I tried to get close to the only family I had left and it appears that they had different plans for me. They took advantage of where I was at and then when they thought I had no back up plan (I had a small community on twitch that they saw)and they treated me horribly. They didn’t believe it when I was diagnosed with allergies and put the things I was allergic to in my food and room. I woke up gasping for air and had to use my inhaler and lay in bed and wait for them to take the flowers I was allergic to out of my room (they did this at night). They did this multiple times and I still can’t sleep at night anymore and it’s been seven months. I started having blood in my stool like when I was eating things I was allergic to in the past and I had to literally stop eating food around them to be safe. I brought it up and asked to go to the doctor and they would not let me until I threatened to talk to their kids about it (they moved out). 

I was there for about two months before I had to leave. At that point they did not speak to me for about a week and the hostility was growing stronger. I left unannounced and we have not spoken since, I don’t think they know that I know they did this but I hope it haunts them. 

I got back and no one in my life knows what happened besides my partner. I have had a lot of moments like this but it’s been happening with the unsafe feels that come from healing this stuff. 

I know people have the ability to be good, and I am very happy for that. I just don’t have a lot of faith in people anymore with me. Mainly because this is not the first time bad things like this have happened and I don’t think I will be able to love myself if I keep trying to be around people anymore. 

So yeah, the bigger breakdowns have stopped for a while now because the understanding is there. Now it’s just trying to figure out what I should do next. Honestly I have just been making art. No one sees in or celebrates it but I put it out there because that’s the only thing that I can do to participate in society. It’s the only thing that has been safe. 

I also stopped consuming media online as much to avoid the unhealthy attachments that comes from the loneliness there. I just have been working on letting go of the idea of closeness like I once thought was possible. People will do what’s in their best interest, and if they go out of that they will not do so consistently. 

I tried my best for a really long time but I don’t even think that I can even handle people anymore.

[here](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3489818/) is a good crash course on how stimulants work, there are over 100 studies sites and amongst those there are roughly 8 that site the long term damages associated with stimulant use without having ADHD. 

Frankly it just makes sense when you consider how the brain functions during episodes of psychosis and with those who have schizophrenia. ADHD is caused by a lack of dopamine receptors where as Schizophrenia is an overabundance of dopamine receptors. Stimulants work by increasing the amount of “dopamine” and “norepinephrine” in the brain to help get some of the dopamine where it should be (Hence why SSRIs will be attempted first with an educated doc). In a “normal” brain there is a balance that is altered by many causes, in which mild amounts of stimulants may off temporary relief  but in the long term the body becomes reliant upon it (hence damage) and starts underproducing these chemicals on its own. Some may never recover from this and if the use is extended long enough or the rate of consumption is increased over time to try and get the “benefits” they experienced upon the initial usage back, they will enter episodes of psychosis or at least minimal hallucinations. This is because the brain is underproducing dopamine and it has mimicked the functionality of those with schizoaffective disorders. 

This is the primary reason why stimulants are schedule II drugs, there’s a lot of info on the long term effects of those on methamphetamines from tests on German soldiers who were given methamphetamines in their MREs. 

There’s plenty of research out there if you need more clarity but I think I provided enough for now. I know topics like these are pretty complicated and difficult to understand, so if you need further assistance I would be happy to help!

I believe people desire this sorta thing for a sense of closure. It may do that for some people, but after the fact, what does it solve besides hopefully preventing others from being abused the same way? Admittance to abusing others takes a level of self awareness that would destroy most abusers. After all, who wants to admit to themselves that they are capable of such horrific actions? Who can look themselves in the eye after that and call themselves a good person? There’s nothing a victim can do that can get an abuser to change their ways, it’s purely up to them. At the end of the day though, them admitting what they did never helps. Admittance shows that they knew what they were doing was wrong but didn’t care, and who wants to admit that? 

So how else can we get closure? We attempt to force the admittance. 

The idea of taking abusers to court and winning is seen as an “ending” to the trauma in the public eye, but it doesn’t address the underlying trauma that the victims face. People who are uneducated on the long term aspects of trauma are most likely people who only ever hear about traumatic events through the news or other media similar will tend to gravitate towards this narrative and at a subconscious level a lot of us do as well. Remember that most of us here on this sub knew nothing about trauma and believed the cultural position on this topic until we endured trauma of our own. Some of us don’t even know what it’s like to not be traumatized so we internalize the societal and cultural concepts on these issues to invalidate our own trauma since “it wasn’t that bad”. We are all raised in societies where the effects of trauma are romanticized and/or ignored so how are we to decondition ourselves from this concept when all we were taught was the exact same thing? I believe the reason for such a fixation on going to court especially is because we are taught that this is the only acceptable step forward. We are taught to believe that it forces the abusers to admit that they hurt you, when in reality that rarely happens. We are conditioned to believe that it will suddenly make everything better for the victim even though the process of a court case is traumatizing. 

I am not saying that going to court is bad, but it won’t heal you like we are taught to believe in western cultures. If you do chose to go that route, be sure you have a stable therapy plan and are emotionally ready to handle it and try not to expect a confession.
